Column: Company
What it means: Supplier name as it appears in the ground truth file.

Column: Ground truth sites
What it means: Distinct (country, city) sites the ground truth holds for this supplier. This is the denominator for both recall figures.

Column: Ground truth rows
What it means: Raw ground-truth rows. Higher than the site count because several rows can describe the same city.

Column: Ground truth rows dropped as invalid
What it means: Rows the ground truth itself marks Validity=Invalid; excluded from every number.

Column: Agent sites / Synapse sites
What it means: Distinct (country, city) sites the system returned for this supplier.

Column: Agent rows returned / Synapse rows returned
What it means: Raw rows in the system's output file, before collapsing to distinct sites.

Column: Agent sites in ground truth / Synapse sites in ground truth
What it means: How many of those sites also appear in the ground truth.

Column: Agent recall % / Synapse recall %
What it means: Sites in ground truth divided by ground truth sites: the share of known sites the system found.

Column: Agent recall % (countries it covered)
What it means: Same, but the denominator is only ground-truth sites in countries the system returned at least one site for, so a system is not charged for geographies it never entered.

Column: Agent sites confirmed by ground truth % / Synapse ...
What it means: Sites in ground truth divided by the system's own sites: how much of its output the ground truth corroborates. Not the same as precision - the ground truth is incomplete, so unconfirmed sites are not necessarily wrong.

Column: Agent addresses matched at street level / Synapse ...
What it means: Stricter check, counted over distinct street addresses rather than cities: the system's street line shares a house number, or half its significant words, with a ground-truth address in the same city.

Column: Agent addresses matched at street level % / Synapse ...
What it means: The above as a share of the system's distinct street addresses.

Column: Agent cost USD
What it means: Estimated model and web-search spend for this supplier, from the last run logged in usage_log.jsonl.

Column: Synapse cost USD
What it means: Left blank - no cost figure for the Synapse/Databricks run exists in this repo.

Column: Sites found by both
What it means: Sites both systems returned.

Column: Overlap % of everything either found
What it means: Sites found by both, divided by the union of both systems' sites.

Column: % of Synapse sites the agent also found
What it means: Sites found by both, divided by Synapse's sites: how much of Synapse the agent reproduces.

Column: Sites found only by agent / only by Synapse
What it means: In this supplier's output, present in one system and absent from the other.

Column: Sites found only by agent and in ground truth
What it means: Of those agent-only sites, how many the ground truth confirms. This is the incremental gain over Synapse.

Column: Sites found only by Synapse and in ground truth
What it means: The same figure for Synapse: what the agent missed and Synapse caught.

Column: Net confirmed sites gained by agent
What it means: Confirmed agent-only sites minus confirmed Synapse-only sites.

Column: Both systems returned sites
What it means: 'no' means one system produced nothing for this supplier, so the head-to-head columns are not meaningful for it.
